details.value: Temporalis, deep temporal nerves and arteries (from V3 and the maxillary artery), middle temporal artery, zygomaticotemporal nerve, branches of the superficial temporal vessels and the auriculotemporal nerve in the overlying fascia

pearl: Blows here fracture the thin pterion and tear the middle meningeal artery (epidural hematoma). Temporal-fossa fullness with jaw pain and trismus suggests a masticator-space abscess; temporalis wasting is a sign of V3 motor loss or chronic illness.

name: Sphenopalatine foramen
function: Opening in the medial wall of the pterygopalatine fossa that leads into the nasal cavity at the back of the superior meatus; carries the sphenopalatine artery and the nasopalatine and posterior lateral nasal nerves.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the orbital and sphenoidal processes of the palatine bone and the body of the sphenoid, at the posterior end of the middle and superior conchae

details.label: Contents
details.value: Sphenopalatine artery and veins (posterior lateral nasal and posterior septal branches), nasopalatine nerve and posterior superior lateral nasal branches from the pterygopalatine ganglion

details.label: Route
details.value: Pterygopalatine fossa → sphenopalatine foramen → lateral nasal wall and septum; the posterior septal branch runs to the incisive canal where it anastomoses with the greater palatine artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Pterygopalatine ganglion lies just lateral to it; maxillary nerve above

pearl: Posterior epistaxis that will not stop with anterior packing comes from the sphenopalatine artery: endoscopic ligation or embolization at this foramen. Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma arises at its margin.

name: Petrotympanic fissure
function: Narrow slit at the back of the mandibular fossa between the tympanic plate and the petrous part of the temporal bone; the exit of the chorda tympani from the middle ear.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posteromedial part of the mandibular fossa, between the tympanic plate and the petrous temporal bone, medial to the external acoustic meatus

details.label: Contents
details.value: Chorda tympani (CN VII) leaving the tympanic cavity to join the lingual nerve in the infratemporal fossa; anterior tympanic artery (maxillary) entering; anterior ligament of the malleus

details.label: Route
details.value: Chorda tympani: facial canal → tympanic cavity across the tympanic membrane → petrotympanic fissure → infratemporal fossa → lingual nerve

details.label: Relations
details.value: Temporomandibular joint capsule in front; spine of the sphenoid and foramen spinosum anteromedial

pearl: Because the chorda tympani leaves through this fissure deep to the TMJ, middle-ear surgery or a fracture of the mandibular fossa can cause loss of taste on the anterior two-thirds of the tongue with reduced salivation.

name: Inferior tympanic canaliculus and mastoid canaliculus
function: Two tiny canals in the jugular region of the skull base: the inferior tympanic canaliculus carries the tympanic nerve of CN IX up into the middle ear, the mastoid canaliculus carries the auricular branch of CN X out to the ear canal.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior tympanic canaliculus: on the ridge between the carotid canal and the jugular fossa; mastoid canaliculus: in the lateral wall of the jugular fossa, opening at the tympanomastoid fissure

details.label: Contents
details.value: Tympanic nerve (of Jacobson, CN IX) with the inferior tympanic artery; auricular branch of the vagus (CN X)

details.label: Route
details.value: Tympanic nerve → promontory and tympanic plexus → lesser petrosal nerve → foramen ovale → otic ganglion; auricular branch of X → facial canal → tympanomastoid fissure → external acoustic meatus and concha

details.label: Relations
details.value: Jugular foramen and internal jugular bulb adjacent; facial nerve in the stylomastoid foramen lateral

pearl: Glomus tympanicum paragangliomas arise from the tympanic plexus on the promontory (pulsatile tinnitus, red mass behind the TM). The auricular branch of X explains cough or syncope when the ear canal is instrumented and referred ear pain from laryngeal cancer.

name: Condylar canal
function: Inconstant canal opening in the condylar fossa behind the occipital condyle; transmits the condylar emissary vein linking the sigmoid sinus with the suboccipital venous plexus and a meningeal branch of the ascending pharyngeal artery.

details.label: Location
details.value: Floor of the condylar fossa immediately posterior to the occipital condyle, opening internally near the sigmoid sinus groove

details.label: Contents
details.value: Condylar emissary vein and meningeal branch of the ascending pharyngeal artery; occasionally a branch of the occipital artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hypoglossal canal lies anterior to the condyle (CN XII); jugular foramen anterolateral; foramen magnum medial

details.label: Distinguish from
details.value: Hypoglossal canal: constant, anterosuperior to the condyle, transmits CN XII and its venous plexus

pearl: Emissary veins such as the condylar vein have no valves, so scalp or suboccipital infection can reach the sigmoid sinus; a large condylar canal is a normal variant on CT, not a fracture.

name: Pterygoid (vidian) canal
function: Canal through the root of the pterygoid process from the anterior margin of the foramen lacerum to the pterygopalatine fossa, carrying the nerve and artery of the pterygoid canal to the pterygopalatine ganglion.

details.label: Location
details.value: Base of the pterygoid process of the sphenoid, running forward from the region of the foramen lacerum to open into the posterior wall of the pterygopalatine fossa

details.label: Contents
details.value: Nerve of the pterygoid canal (vidian nerve = greater petrosal nerve + deep petrosal nerve) and the artery of the pterygoid canal (from the third part of the maxillary artery, with a branch from the petrous internal carotid)

details.label: Route
details.value: Greater petrosal (parasympathetic, from the geniculate ganglion) crosses the foramen lacerum and joins the deep petrosal (sympathetic, from the internal carotid plexus) → pterygoid canal → pterygopalatine ganglion → lacrimal gland, nasal and palatal glands

details.label: Relations
details.value: Foramen rotundum lies above and lateral; the sphenoid sinus floor is above the canal

pearl: A lesion of CN VII proximal to the geniculate ganglion (or vidian nerve surgery) abolishes reflex tearing on that side; vidian neurectomy was used for intractable vasomotor rhinitis. The canal is the landmark for the petrous ICA in endoscopic skull-base surgery.

name: Sphenoidal emissary foramen (of Vesalius)
function: Inconstant small foramen in the greater wing of the sphenoid, anteromedial to the foramen ovale, through which an emissary vein joins the cavernous sinus to the pterygoid venous plexus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Greater wing of the sphenoid, anteromedial to the foramen ovale and lateral to the foramen rotundum; present in a minority of skulls (Netter: inconstant)

details.label: Contents
details.value: Sphenoidal emissary vein (of Vesalius) connecting the cavernous sinus with the pterygoid plexus

details.label: Related venous links
details.value: Emissary veins also pass through the foramen ovale and foramen lacerum to the pterygoid plexus; the deep facial vein then links the plexus to the facial vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: V3 at the foramen ovale posterolateral; V2 at the foramen rotundum anteromedial

pearl: Valveless emissary veins through this foramen and the foramen ovale let infection of the deep face, teeth or pterygoid plexus reach the cavernous sinus (cavernous sinus thrombosis with CN VI palsy first).

name: Hiatuses for the greater and lesser petrosal nerves
function: Two small openings on the anterior surface of the petrous temporal bone in the floor of the middle cranial fossa, each leading into a groove that carries a petrosal nerve forward.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior surface of the petrous part of the temporal bone, lateral to the trigeminal impression; the greater hiatus and groove run toward the foramen lacerum, the lesser hiatus and groove lie lateral to them and run toward the foramen ovale

details.label: Contents
details.value: Greater petrosal nerve (from the geniculate ganglion of CN VII, parasympathetic for the lacrimal, nasal and palatine glands); lesser petrosal nerve (from the tympanic plexus of CN IX, parasympathetic for the parotid)

details.label: Route
details.value: Greater petrosal: hiatus → groove → under the trigeminal ganglion → foramen lacerum → pterygoid canal; lesser petrosal: hiatus → groove → foramen ovale → otic ganglion

details.label: Relations
details.value: Arcuate eminence (anterior semicircular canal) posterolateral; tegmen tympani lateral; middle meningeal artery crosses the floor anterolaterally

pearl: Middle cranial fossa fractures or surgery along the petrous ridge can injure the greater petrosal nerve (dry eye, loss of nasal secretion) or the lesser petrosal nerve; Frey syndrome after parotidectomy involves the same lesser-petrosal parasympathetic fibers regrowing into sweat glands.

name: Foramen cecum and crista galli
function: Midline landmarks at the front of the anterior cranial fossa: the crista galli is the upward projection of the ethmoid that anchors the falx cerebri, and the foramen cecum just in front of it transmits an emissary vein to the superior sagittal sinus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Crista galli rises from the cribriform plate between the two olfactory bulbs; the foramen cecum lies between the frontal crest of the frontal bone and the crista galli

details.label: Contents
details.value: Foramen cecum: emissary vein from the nasal cavity to the superior sagittal sinus (often closed in adults); crista galli: attachment of the falx cerebri

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cribriform plate with the olfactory nerves on each side; frontal sinus anterior; the groove for the superior sagittal sinus begins at the frontal crest

details.label: Development
details.value: The foramen cecum marks the embryonic tract between skin and dura through which nasal dermoids and encephaloceles can extend

pearl: A midline nasal pit or mass in an infant (nasal dermoid, glioma or encephalocele) may track through the foramen cecum to the dura: image before any biopsy or incision. Falx attachment at the crista galli is why anterior fossa meningiomas can be bilateral.

name: Anterior and posterior ethmoidal foramina
function: Two small openings in the medial orbital wall at the frontoethmoidal suture that carry the ethmoidal vessels and nerves from the orbit into the anterior cranial fossa and nasal cavity.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial wall of the orbit between the frontal bone and the orbital plate of the ethmoid; the posterior foramen lies close to the optic canal

details.label: Contents
details.value: Anterior ethmoidal artery, vein and nerve (from the ophthalmic artery and nasociliary nerve); posterior ethmoidal artery, vein and nerve

details.label: Route
details.value: Anterior ethmoidal bundle → anterior cranial fossa beside the cribriform plate → nasal slit → anterior nasal cavity and external nose; posterior bundle → posterior ethmoidal cells and sphenoid sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Orbital plate of the ethmoid (lamina papyracea) below and behind; medial rectus; the optic canal is posterior to the posterior foramen

pearl: The anterior ethmoidal artery is the vessel torn in medial orbital wall fractures and in endoscopic sinus surgery: it retracts into the orbit and causes a rapidly expanding retrobulbar hematoma needing urgent lateral canthotomy. It also feeds Kiesselbach plexus epistaxis.

name: Clivus and pharyngeal tubercle
function: The clivus is the sloping midline surface formed by the sphenoid body and the basilar part of the occipital bone, running from the dorsum sellae to the foramen magnum; the pharyngeal tubercle on its undersurface anchors the pharynx to the skull.

details.label: Location
details.value: Clivus: posterior cranial fossa floor behind the sella, flanked by the grooves for the inferior petrosal sinuses; pharyngeal tubercle: inferior surface of the basilar occipital bone in front of the foramen magnum

details.label: Relations (intracranial)
details.value: Pons and basilar artery lie on the clivus; basilar venous plexus on its dura; CN VI ascends on it; the tectorial membrane and apical ligament of the dens attach to its lower end

details.label: Attachments (external)
details.value: Pharyngeal raphe, superior pharyngeal constrictor and pharyngobasilar fascia to the pharyngeal tubercle; longus capitis and rectus capitis anterior lateral to it; anterior atlanto-occipital membrane and anterior longitudinal ligament below

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Spheno-occipital synchondrosis between sphenoid body and basilar occipital bone

pearl: Chordoma, a midline tumor of notochord remnants, arises in the clivus and causes headache with a CN VI palsy; nasopharyngeal carcinoma erodes the clivus from below. The spheno-occipital synchondrosis fuses in late adolescence, so clival growth is a radiographic age marker.

name: Occipital condyles, nuchal lines and external occipital crest
function: The occipital condyles are the paired convex facets beside the foramen magnum that rock on the atlas; the nuchal lines and external occipital crest behind them are the attachment ridges for the posterior neck muscles and the nuchal ligament.

details.label: Occipital condyles
details.value: On the lateral parts of the occipital bone, converging anteriorly; articulate with the superior articular surfaces of the lateral masses of the atlas (atlanto-occipital joint: flexion and extension); hypoglossal canal passes above the anterior half, condylar fossa and canal lie behind

details.label: Superior nuchal line
details.value: From the external occipital protuberance laterally to the mastoid; trapezius and occipital belly of occipitofrontalis above, sternocleidomastoid and splenius capitis below

details.label: Inferior nuchal line
details.value: Lower ridge for rectus capitis posterior major and minor and obliquus capitis superior (suboccipital muscles); semispinalis capitis attaches between the two lines

details.label: External occipital crest
details.value: Midline ridge from the protuberance to the foramen magnum for the nuchal ligament; jugular process projects lateral to the condyle for rectus capitis lateralis

pearl: Occipital condyle fractures (high-energy trauma) present with occipital pain and a CN XII palsy from hypoglossal canal involvement; atlanto-occipital dissociation is often fatal. Tenderness along the superior nuchal line with occipital headache suggests greater occipital neuralgia.

name: Posterior, sphenoidal and mastoid fontanelles (newborn skull)
function: Membranous gaps at the corners of the parietal bones in the newborn skull that allow moulding at birth and brain growth; the posterior fontanelle lies at the lambda, the sphenoidal and mastoid fontanelles at the lateral suture junctions.

details.label: Posterior fontanelle
details.value: Triangular, between the two parietal bones and the occipital bone at the lambda (sagittal and lambdoid sutures)

details.label: Sphenoidal fontanelle
details.value: Lateral, where the frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and greater wing of the sphenoid meet; becomes the pterion

details.label: Mastoid fontanelle
details.value: Posterolateral, between the parietal, occipital and temporal bones; becomes the asterion; the mastoid process is absent at birth so the facial nerve is superficial

details.label: Metopic suture
details.value: Midline suture between the two halves of the frontal bone in the newborn; normally fuses in early childhood

pearl: A wide or late-closing posterior fontanelle points to congenital hypothyroidism or Down syndrome; bulging fontanelles mean raised ICP, sunken ones dehydration. Premature fusion of the metopic suture gives trigonocephaly; without a mastoid process the newborn facial nerve is exposed in forceps delivery.

name: Bregma, lambda, asterion and sutural (wormian) bones
function: Named points where cranial sutures meet: the bregma (coronal–sagittal) and lambda (sagittal–lambdoid) mark the sites of the anterior and posterior fontanelles, and the asterion marks the lateral end of the lambdoid suture over the transverse–sigmoid sinus junction.

details.label: Bregma
details.value: Junction of the coronal and sagittal sutures on the vertex; site of the anterior fontanelle

details.label: Lambda
details.value: Junction of the sagittal and lambdoid sutures; site of the posterior fontanelle; sutural (wormian) bones are commonest along the lambdoid suture

details.label: Asterion
details.value: Junction of the lambdoid, occipitomastoid and parietomastoid sutures behind the mastoid; overlies the junction of the transverse and sigmoid sinuses

details.label: Sutural (wormian) bones
details.value: Accessory ossicles within sutures, usually lambdoid; a few are normal, many suggest a bone dysplasia

pearl: Numerous wormian bones are a radiographic clue to osteogenesis imperfecta, cleidocranial dysplasia, hypothyroidism, rickets or Down syndrome. The asterion is the surgical landmark for the sigmoid sinus in retrosigmoid craniotomy; the pterion (sphenoidal fontanelle) overlies the middle meningeal artery.

name: Mandibular fossa and articular tubercle
function: The temporal bone's part of the temporomandibular joint: the concave mandibular fossa receives the condyle at rest and the articular tubercle in front is the ridge the condyle and disc glide onto when the mouth opens wide.

details.label: Location
details.value: Squamous temporal bone at the root of the zygomatic process, in front of the external acoustic meatus and tympanic plate; the petrotympanic fissure crosses the back of the fossa

details.label: Key features
details.value: Fossa floored by thin bone separating it from the middle cranial fossa; articular tubercle anterior; postglenoid tubercle behind; fibrocartilage-covered surfaces with the articular disc between

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Joint capsule around the fossa and tubercle; lateral (temporomandibular) ligament from the tubercle and zygomatic arch to the condylar neck

details.label: Movement
details.value: Hinge rotation in the lower compartment; with wide opening the condyle and disc translate forward onto the tubercle, pulled by the lateral pterygoid

pearl: Anterior TMJ dislocation (yawning, extubation) leaves the condyle stuck in front of the articular tubercle: open mouth that will not close; reduce with downward then backward thumb pressure on the lower molars. A blow to the chin can drive the condyle through the thin fossa into the middle fossa.

name: Pterygomandibular raphe
function: Tendinous band stretching from the pterygoid hamulus to the mandible behind the last molar; the buccinator attaches to its front and the superior pharyngeal constrictor to its back, so it joins the cheek to the pharynx.

details.label: Location
details.value: From the hamulus of the medial pterygoid plate to the posterior end of the mylohyoid line of the mandible, deep to the mucosa behind the third molar

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Buccinator anteriorly; superior pharyngeal constrictor posteriorly

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lingual nerve and buccal artery and nerve pass nearby in the infratemporal fossa; palatoglossal fold medial; the ramus and medial pterygoid lateral

details.label: Clinical landmark
details.value: Visible as a mucosal ridge when the mouth is open wide; marks the needle entry for an inferior alveolar nerve block just lateral to it

pearl: The inferior alveolar nerve block is placed lateral to the pterygomandibular raphe at the level of the occlusal plane; the raphe is also the lateral boundary of the peritonsillar space, so peritonsillar abscess causes trismus by irritating the adjacent medial pterygoid.

name: Uncovertebral joints (clefts of Luschka) and uncinate processes
function: Small joints between the upward-projecting uncinate processes on the lateral edges of the C3–C7 vertebral bodies and the bevelled inferior margins of the vertebra above; they guide flexion–extension and are the first cervical joints to degenerate.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral edges of the superior surfaces of the bodies of C3–C7 (and the top of T1), immediately medial to the transverse foramen and in front of the intervertebral foramen

details.label: Structure
details.value: Uncinate process of the lower vertebra meets the lower body of the upper vertebra; cleft-like cavities form in the disc margin with age (clefts of Luschka)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Vertebral artery in the transverse foramen lateral; spinal nerve in the intervertebral foramen posterolateral; intervertebral disc medial

details.label: Degeneration
details.value: Osteophytes (spondylophytes) on the uncinate processes narrow the intervertebral foramen and may compress the vertebral artery

pearl: Cervical spondylosis: uncovertebral osteophytes narrow the intervertebral foramina and cause radiculopathy (C6 and C7 roots most often); the same osteophytes can compress the vertebral artery in the transverse foramen, causing vertigo on neck rotation. On an oblique radiograph, foraminal narrowing is an uncovertebral finding.

name: Carotid tubercle (of Chassaignac, C6)
function: Enlarged anterior tubercle of the transverse process of C6 against which the common carotid artery can be compressed; a landmark for the C6 level and for the stellate ganglion block.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior tubercle of the transverse process of C6, palpable lateral to the cricoid cartilage

details.label: Relations
details.value: Common carotid artery and carotid sheath in front; vertebral artery entering the transverse foramen of C6 just above; longus colli and the sympathetic trunk medial; inferior thyroid artery and middle cervical ganglion nearby

details.label: C6 level
details.value: Cricoid cartilage, larynx becoming trachea, pharynx becoming esophagus, omohyoid crossing the carotid sheath, vertebral artery entry

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Longus colli and anterior scalene slips attach to the anterior tubercles

pearl: Stellate ganglion block is placed at the carotid tubercle with the carotid retracted laterally; complications include Horner syndrome (expected), hoarseness, and intra-arterial vertebral injection with seizures. The tubercle is where the carotid pulse can be occluded by direct pressure.

name: Transverse ligament of the atlas and cruciate ligament
function: Strong band between the lateral masses of the atlas that holds the dens against the anterior arch; with its superior and inferior longitudinal bands it forms the cruciate ligament, the main restraint against atlantoaxial subluxation.

details.label: Transverse ligament
details.value: From the tubercle on one lateral mass of the atlas to the other, behind the dens; synovial cavities lie in front (dens–anterior arch) and behind (dens–ligament); the posterior articular facet of the dens faces it

details.label: Cruciate ligament
details.value: Transverse ligament plus a superior longitudinal band to the clivus and an inferior band to the body of the axis

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tectorial membrane and dura behind; alar and apical ligaments in front and above; spinal cord immediately posterior

details.label: Function
details.value: Permits rotation at the median atlantoaxial joint while preventing the dens from moving back into the cord

pearl: Rupture or laxity (Down syndrome, rheumatoid pannus, retropharyngeal infection in children) lets the dens compress the cord: an atlantodental interval widened on a flexion lateral film. Screen Down syndrome children before contact sports; a Jefferson burst fracture is unstable when the transverse ligament is torn.

name: Alar and apical ligaments, tectorial membrane and atlanto-occipital membranes
function: Set of craniocervical ligaments joining the dens and the atlas to the occiput: the alar ligaments check rotation, the apical ligament tethers the tip of the dens, the tectorial membrane continues the posterior longitudinal ligament onto the clivus, and the atlanto-occipital membranes close the joint front and back.

details.label: Alar ligaments
details.value: From the sides of the apex of the dens upward and laterally to the medial surfaces of the occipital condyles; limit rotation and lateral flexion of the head (check ligaments)

details.label: Apical ligament
details.value: From the apex of the dens to the anterior margin of the foramen magnum (basion), between the alar ligaments

details.label: Tectorial membrane
details.value: Upward continuation of the posterior longitudinal ligament from the body of the axis over the dens and cruciate ligament to the clivus; a deeper accessory part forms the atlantoaxial ligament

details.label: Atlanto-occipital membranes and nuchal ligament
details.value: Anterior membrane from the anterior arch of the atlas to the basilar occipital bone (with the anterior longitudinal ligament); posterior membrane from the posterior arch to the foramen magnum, pierced by the vertebral artery and suboccipital nerve; nuchal ligament from the C7 spine and supraspinous ligament to the external occipital crest and protuberance

pearl: Alar ligament tears from rotational trauma (whiplash, rugby) cause upper cervical instability seen on flexion–extension MRI; in rheumatoid arthritis and Down syndrome, laxity of these ligaments plus the transverse ligament allows cranial settling of the dens into the foramen magnum.

name: Corniculate, cuneiform and triticeal cartilages
function: Minor laryngeal cartilages: the corniculate cartilages sit on the apex of each arytenoid, the cuneiform cartilages lie in the aryepiglottic folds in front of them, and the triticeal cartilage is a nodule in the lateral thyrohyoid ligament.

details.label: Corniculate cartilages
details.value: Small elastic nodules on the apices of the arytenoid cartilages, seen as the corniculate tubercles at the back of the aryepiglottic folds

details.label: Cuneiform cartilages
details.value: Elastic rods in the aryepiglottic folds anterolateral to the corniculate cartilages, forming the cuneiform tubercles

details.label: Triticeal cartilage
details.value: Grain-of-wheat nodule in the lateral thyrohyoid ligament between the superior horn of the thyroid cartilage and the greater horn of the hyoid (inconstant)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Aryepiglottic fold with the aryepiglottic part of the oblique arytenoid; piriform recess lateral; laryngeal inlet in front

pearl: On laryngoscopy the paired corniculate and cuneiform tubercles mark the posterior rim of the laryngeal inlet and help identify the arytenoids before passing the tube. A calcified triticeal cartilage on a lateral neck film can mimic a swallowed bone or a carotid plaque.

name: Median cricothyroid ligament, conus elasticus and cricothyroid joint
function: Elastic membrane filling the gap between the cricoid arch and the thyroid cartilage: its thickened anterior midline part is the median cricothyroid ligament (the cricothyrotomy site), and its lateral part, the conus elasticus, rises to a free edge that is the vocal ligament.

details.label: Median cricothyroid ligament
details.value: Midline band from the upper border of the cricoid arch to the inferior border of the thyroid cartilage, subcutaneous between the cricothyroid muscles

details.label: Conus elasticus
details.value: Lateral cricothyroid membrane from the arch of the cricoid up to the vocal ligament, which runs from the vocal process of the arytenoid to the inner angle of the thyroid cartilage; forms the wall of the infraglottic cavity under the vocalis

details.label: Cricothyroid joint
details.value: Synovial joint between the inferior horn of the thyroid cartilage and the side of the cricoid; the thyroid tilts forward on it (cricothyroid muscle), lengthening and tensing the vocal ligaments

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cricothyroid artery (superior thyroid) crosses the ligament; recurrent laryngeal nerve enters the larynx behind the cricothyroid joint; thyroid isthmus lies just below the cricoid

pearl: Emergency cricothyrotomy: stabilize the thyroid cartilage, incise skin and the median cricothyroid ligament in the midline below the laryngeal prominence (Netter Table 2.1: thyroid and cricoid cartilages are the palpable landmarks). Avoid in children under about 10, where needle cricothyrotomy is used; the recurrent laryngeal nerve is vulnerable at the cricothyroid joint during thyroidectomy.

name: Thyrohyoid membrane
function: Fibroelastic sheet suspending the larynx from the hyoid bone; thickened in the midline (median thyrohyoid ligament) and at its posterior borders (lateral thyrohyoid ligaments), and pierced on each side by the internal laryngeal nerve and superior laryngeal vessels.

details.label: Attachments
details.value: From the upper border of the thyroid cartilage laminae and superior horns up to the posterior surface of the body and greater horns of the hyoid

details.label: Key features
details.value: Median thyrohyoid ligament anteriorly; lateral thyrohyoid ligaments posteriorly containing the triticeal cartilage; a foramen on each side for the superior laryngeal vessels and the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve

details.label: Relations
details.value: Thyrohyoid muscle and the infrahyoid strap muscles in front; epiglottis, pre-epiglottic fat and piriform recess behind; a bursa separates it from the hyoid body

details.label: Pierced by
details.value: Internal laryngeal nerve (sensation above the vocal folds) and superior laryngeal artery and vein

pearl: Superior laryngeal nerve block for awake intubation is placed where the internal branch pierces the membrane below the greater horn of the hyoid. A laryngocele (air sac from the laryngeal ventricle) herniates through this membrane as a neck mass that enlarges on Valsalva; a thyroglossal duct cyst lies in front of it.

name: Tympanic membrane (pars tensa, pars flaccida, umbo)
function: Oval, cone-shaped membrane closing the medial end of the external acoustic meatus; the handle of the malleus is embedded in it and pulls its centre, the umbo, medially. The taut pars tensa vibrates with sound; the small pars flaccida lies above the lateral process of the malleus.

details.label: Key features
details.value: Pars tensa (lower, taut, three-layered); pars flaccida (above the anterior and posterior mallear folds); umbo at the tip of the handle of the malleus; lateral process of the malleus; cone of light reflecting anteroinferiorly on otoscopy

details.label: Layers
details.value: Outer skin continuous with the meatus, middle fibrous layer (absent in the pars flaccida), inner mucosa of the tympanic cavity

details.label: Relations
details.value: Chorda tympani crosses its medial surface between the handle of the malleus and the long limb of the incus; auditory tube opens anteriorly; facial nerve posterosuperior

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Outer surface: auriculotemporal nerve (V3) and auricular branch of X; inner surface: tympanic plexus (CN IX)

pearl: Acute otitis media: bulging, erythematous TM with loss of landmarks and no mobility on pneumatic otoscopy. A retraction pocket in the pars flaccida is the origin of cholesteatoma. Traumatic perforations usually heal; a perforation with foul discharge and hearing loss needs ENT review.

name: Tympanic cavity landmarks (promontory, pyramidal eminence, tegmen tympani, epitympanic recess, mastoid antrum)
function: Named landmarks of the walls of the middle ear: the promontory and windows of the medial (labyrinthine) wall, the pyramidal eminence and facial-canal prominence posteriorly, the tegmen tympani roof, the epitympanic recess above the membrane and the aditus leading back to the mastoid antrum.

details.label: Medial (labyrinthine) wall
details.value: Promontory (basal turn of the cochlea) carrying the tympanic nerve of Jacobson and tympanic plexus; vestibular (oval) window above and behind it holding the stapes footplate; fossa of the cochlear (round) window below; prominence of the facial canal and of the lateral semicircular canal above

details.label: Posterior wall
details.value: Pyramidal eminence giving the stapedius tendon; chorda tympani entering nearby; aditus to the mastoid antrum and mastoid air cells behind the epitympanic recess

details.label: Roof and floor
details.value: Tegmen tympani: thin plate of petrous bone separating the cavity and antrum from the middle cranial fossa dura; floor: thin bone over the jugular fossa (jugular bulb)

details.label: Anterior wall and epitympanic recess
details.value: Carotid canal with the caroticotympanic nerves and artery; openings of the auditory tube and tensor tympani canal; epitympanic recess (attic) above the tympanic membrane houses the head of the malleus and body of the incus

pearl: Cholesteatoma in the attic erodes the lateral semicircular canal (fistula with vertigo), the facial canal (facial palsy) and the tegmen (meningitis, brain abscess). Acute mastoiditis spreads from the antrum through the mastoid cortex: postauricular swelling pushing the ear forward. A red pulsatile mass on the promontory is a glomus tympanicum.

name: Oval (vestibular) and round (cochlear) windows
function: The two openings between the middle and inner ear on the labyrinthine wall: the oval window is closed by the footplate of the stapes and transmits vibration into the perilymph of the vestibule and scala vestibuli, while the round window, sealed by the secondary tympanic membrane, lets the scala tympani bulge outward in return.

details.label: Oval (vestibular) window
details.value: Above and behind the promontory; occupied by the base of the stapes held by the annular ligament; opens into the vestibule and scala vestibuli

details.label: Round (cochlear) window
details.value: In the fossa below and behind the promontory; closed by the secondary tympanic membrane; ends the scala tympani at the basal turn of the cochlea

details.label: Mechanics
details.value: Stapes footplate pushes perilymph through the scala vestibuli → helicotrema → scala tympani; the round window membrane yields so fluid can move and the basilar membrane can vibrate

details.label: Relations
details.value: Facial nerve in its canal just above the oval window; stapedius tendon from the pyramidal eminence to the stapes neck; tympanic plexus on the promontory between the windows

pearl: Otosclerosis fixes the stapes footplate in the oval window: progressive conductive hearing loss in a young adult with a normal TM and a Carhart notch; treated by stapedectomy. Perilymph fistula at either window after barotrauma or stapes surgery causes fluctuating hearing loss and vertigo.

name: Bony labyrinth (cochlea, vestibule, semicircular canals, arcuate eminence)
function: Series of cavities in the petrous temporal bone (otic capsule) filled with perilymph that house the membranous labyrinth: the cochlea anteriorly for hearing, the vestibule centrally for the utricle and saccule, and the three semicircular canals posteriorly for angular acceleration.

details.label: Cochlea
details.value: Spiral canal around the modiolus; the osseous spiral lamina and basilar membrane divide it into scala vestibuli and scala tympani, meeting at the helicotrema; its basal turn forms the promontory of the middle ear

details.label: Vestibule
details.value: Central chamber behind the cochlea with the elliptical recess (utricle) and spherical recess (saccule); the oval window opens into its lateral wall; the vestibular aqueduct runs from it to the posterior petrous surface carrying the endolymphatic duct to the endolymphatic sac under the dura

details.label: Semicircular canals
details.value: Anterior (under the arcuate eminence of the petrous ridge), posterior and lateral canals, each with an ampulla; anterior and posterior share a common bony limb; the lateral canal bulges into the middle ear above the facial canal

details.label: Relations
details.value: Internal acoustic meatus medial (CN VII, CN VIII, labyrinthine artery); facial nerve passes between cochlea and vestibule to the geniculate ganglion; cochlear aqueduct links the scala tympani to the subarachnoid space

pearl: Posterior canal BPPV: otoconia from the utricle enter the posterior semicircular canal, giving brief rotatory vertigo on Dix–Hallpike, cured by the Epley manoeuvre. Ménière disease is endolymphatic hydrops. Transverse petrous fractures cross the labyrinth and cause sensorineural deafness and vertigo; longitudinal fractures spare it but tear the TM.

name: Nasal cartilages (septal, lateral process, major and minor alar)
function: Hyaline and elastic cartilages forming the lower two-thirds of the external nose: the septal cartilage in the midline with its lateral processes forming the dorsum, and the paired major alar cartilages (lateral and medial crura) shaping the tip and nostrils.

details.label: Septal nasal cartilage
details.value: Quadrangular plate between the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid and the vomer, resting on the anterior nasal spine and maxillary crest; its lateral processes (upper lateral cartilages) extend onto the dorsum beneath the nasal bones

details.label: Major alar cartilages
details.value: U-shaped, with a lateral crus forming the ala and a medial crus forming the columella; the alar fibrofatty tissue completes the ala posteriorly

details.label: Minor alar and accessory cartilages
details.value: Small plates between the lateral process and the major alar cartilage

details.label: Relations
details.value: Nasalis (transverse and alar parts) and depressor septi nasi over the cartilages; external nasal nerve and artery emerge between the nasal bone and the lateral process; lateral nasal artery of the facial artery supplies the ala

pearl: After nasal trauma look for a septal hematoma (boggy bilateral septal swelling): drain it promptly, because the cartilage is nourished by the perichondrium and will necrose, leaving a saddle-nose deformity. Cocaine and granulomatosis with polyangiitis perforate the septal cartilage.

name: Lateral nasal wall: meatuses, semilunar hiatus, ethmoidal bulla, uncinate process, sphenoethmoidal recess, agger nasi
function: Drainage map of the lateral nasal wall: each sinus opens into a named recess under a concha. The osteomeatal unit in the middle meatus (uncinate process, semilunar hiatus, ethmoidal bulla, infundibulum) drains the frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoid sinuses.

details.label: Sphenoethmoidal recess and superior meatus
details.value: Recess above the superior concha receives the opening of the sphenoidal sinus; the superior meatus receives the posterior ethmoidal cells; the sphenopalatine foramen lies behind the middle concha

details.label: Middle meatus (osteomeatal unit)
details.value: Ethmoidal bulla (middle ethmoidal cells open on it); semilunar hiatus below the bulla receives the frontonasal duct (frontal sinus) via the infundibulum, the anterior ethmoidal cells and the maxillary sinus opening; the uncinate process forms its lower lip

details.label: Inferior meatus and agger nasi
details.value: Nasolacrimal duct opens under the inferior concha; the agger nasi is the ridge in front of the middle concha over the anterior ethmoidal cells, the landmark for the frontal recess

details.label: Relations
details.value: Orbit (orbital plate of the ethmoid) lateral to the ethmoidal cells; maxillary sinus lateral to the middle and inferior meatuses; cribriform plate above

pearl: Obstruction of the osteomeatal complex by mucosal oedema, polyps or a deviated septum causes maxillary, frontal and anterior ethmoid sinusitis together; functional endoscopic sinus surgery removes the uncinate process and bulla to reopen it. Nasolacrimal duct obstruction gives epiphora; congenital obstruction presents as a dacryocystocele in the inferior meatus.

name: Squamous part of temporal bone
function: Thin, fan-shaped plate forming the lower lateral wall of the cranial vault and part of the middle cranial fossa; it carries the zygomatic process and the socket of the temporomandibular joint.

details.label: Location
details.value: Side of the skull above the external acoustic meatus, overlapped by the parietal bone at the squamous suture and meeting the greater wing of the sphenoid in front

details.label: Key features
details.value: Zygomatic process, articular tubercle, mandibular fossa, supramastoid crest, groove for the posterior deep temporal artery; inner surface grooved by the middle meningeal vessels

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Temporalis (floor of the temporal fossa), temporal fascia (supramastoid crest and zygomatic process), masseter (zygomatic process), capsule and lateral ligament of the TMJ (articular tubercle)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Temporal lobe and middle meningeal vessels medially; superficial temporal vessels and auriculotemporal nerve laterally

pearl: A blow to the thin squamous temporal bone can tear the middle meningeal artery and cause an epidural hematoma: lucid interval, then a lens-shaped bleed on CT.

name: Petrous part of temporal bone
function: Dense pyramid of bone wedged between the sphenoid and occipital bones in the skull base; it houses the inner ear, the facial canal and the carotid canal, and its ridge separates the middle from the posterior cranial fossa. The mastoid process is its postnatal downgrowth.

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs anteromedially from the mastoid region to the foramen lacerum; anterior surface in the middle cranial fossa, posterior surface in the posterior cranial fossa, inferior surface on the external cranial base

details.label: Key features
details.value: Arcuate eminence, trigeminal impression, grooves for the greater and lesser petrosal nerves, groove for the superior petrosal sinus along its ridge, internal acoustic meatus, opening of the vestibular aqueduct, groove for the sigmoid sinus, jugular fossa, external opening of the carotid canal, mastoid process and mastoid notch, groove for the occipital artery

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Internal acoustic meatus – CN VII, CN VIII, labyrinthine artery; carotid canal – internal carotid artery and plexus; stylomastoid foramen – CN VII; mastoid canaliculus – auricular branch of CN X; inferior tympanic canaliculus – tympanic nerve (CN IX)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Tentorium cerebelli (petrous ridge), levator veli palatini (inferior surface), cartilage of the auditory tube (groove between petrous part and greater wing)

pearl: Petrous apicitis complicating otitis media gives Gradenigo syndrome: ear discharge, deep facial (trigeminal) pain and abducens palsy.

name: Tympanic part of temporal bone
function: Curved plate of bone below the squamous part that forms the anterior wall, floor and part of the posterior wall of the bony external acoustic meatus and sheathes the root of the styloid process.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the mandibular fossa in front and the mastoid process behind; separated from the mandibular fossa by the petrotympanic fissure

details.label: Key features
details.value: Bony external acoustic meatus; tympanic sulcus for the tympanic membrane; at birth it is only an incomplete ring, so the bony meatus is absent and the tympanic membrane lies near the surface

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Petrotympanic fissure – chorda tympani and anterior tympanic artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Head of the mandible and parotid gland anteriorly; styloid process and stylomastoid foramen (CN VII) posteroinferiorly

pearl: In the newborn the bony meatus and mastoid process are absent, so the facial nerve leaves the stylomastoid foramen close to the surface and can be injured by forceps or a postauricular incision.

name: Greater wing of sphenoid bone
function: Large lateral wing of the sphenoid that forms the floor of the middle cranial fossa, the lateral wall of the orbit and the roof of the infratemporal fossa; it transmits the maxillary and mandibular nerves and the middle meningeal artery.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Cerebral surface (middle cranial fossa, temporal lobe); orbital surface (lateral wall of orbit); temporal surface (temporal fossa, pterion); infratemporal surface below the infratemporal crest (roof of infratemporal fossa); spine of the sphenoid posteriorly

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Foramen rotundum – V2; foramen ovale – V3, accessory meningeal artery, lesser petrosal nerve; foramen spinosum – middle meningeal vessels and meningeal branch of V3; sphenoidal emissary foramen (inconstant)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Temporalis (temporal surface), upper head of lateral pterygoid (infratemporal surface and crest), sphenomandibular ligament and tensor veli palatini (spine)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Bounds the superior orbital fissure (with the lesser wing) and the inferior orbital fissure (with the maxilla); meets frontal, parietal and temporal bones at the pterion

pearl: The greater wing is the thin floor of the pterion: fracture here tears the frontal branch of the middle meningeal artery and causes an epidural hematoma.

name: Lesser wing of sphenoid bone
function: Thin triangular plate projecting laterally from the front of the sphenoid body; it forms the posterior edge of the anterior cranial fossa and the roof of the orbital apex, and encloses the optic canal.

details.label: Location
details.value: Above the superior orbital fissure, between the orbital part of the frontal bone in front and the greater wing below

details.label: Key features
details.value: Anterior clinoid process at its medial end; optic canal between its two roots; orbital surface forming the posterior orbital roof; sharp posterior border (sphenoid ridge) fitting the lateral sulcus of the brain

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Optic canal – optic nerve (CN II) and ophthalmic artery; superior orbital fissure (between lesser and greater wings) – CN III, IV, VI, branches of V1, superior ophthalmic vein

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Free edge of the tentorium cerebelli (anterior clinoid process); levator palpebrae superioris and the common tendinous ring near the optic canal

pearl: A sphenoid wing meningioma causes painless proptosis and progressive visual loss by narrowing the optic canal and superior orbital fissure.

name: Perpendicular plate of ethmoid bone
function: Thin midline plate hanging from the cribriform plate that forms the upper part of the bony nasal septum.

details.label: Location
details.value: Midline of the nasal cavity, continuous above with the crista galli

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal bone (nasal spine) and nasal bones in front, crest and body of the sphenoid behind, vomer posteroinferiorly, septal nasal cartilage anteroinferiorly

details.label: Key features
details.value: Upper edge grooved by olfactory nerve filaments descending from the cribriform plate

details.label: Relations
details.value: Olfactory mucosa on its upper part; anterior ethmoidal nerve and vessels and the posterior septal branches of the sphenopalatine artery supply its mucosa

pearl: Twisting the perpendicular plate during septal surgery or nasal trauma can crack the cribriform plate and cause CSF rhinorrhea and anosmia.

name: Orbital plate of ethmoid bone (lamina papyracea)
function: Paper-thin lateral wall of the ethmoidal labyrinth that forms most of the medial wall of the orbit and separates the orbit from the ethmoidal cells.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial orbital wall, between the lacrimal bone in front and the body of the sphenoid behind, below the orbital part of the frontal bone and above the orbital surface of the maxilla

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Anterior and posterior ethmoidal foramina in the fronto-ethmoidal suture – anterior and posterior ethmoidal nerves and vessels

details.label: Key features
details.value: Thinnest wall of the orbit; ethmoidal cells lie directly behind it

details.label: Relations
details.value: Medial rectus and superior oblique laterally; ethmoidal cells medially; optic canal just behind the posterior ethmoidal foramen

pearl: Ethmoid sinusitis spreads through the orbital plate to cause orbital cellulitis, and a medial-wall blowout fracture lets air into the orbit (orbital emphysema after nose blowing).

name: Superior and middle nasal conchae (and highest nasal concha)
function: Scroll-like projections of the ethmoidal labyrinth on the lateral nasal wall that increase mucosal surface area and roof the superior and middle meatuses; unlike the inferior concha they are parts of the ethmoid bone, not separate bones.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Highest nasal concha (inconstant, above the superior); superior nasal concha (roofs the superior meatus, sphenoethmoidal recess above it); middle nasal concha (roofs the middle meatus, covers the ethmoidal bulla, uncinate process and semilunar hiatus)

details.label: Location
details.value: Upper lateral wall of the nasal cavity, above the inferior nasal concha and below the cribriform plate

details.label: Key features
details.value: Superior meatus receives the posterior ethmoidal cells; middle meatus receives the frontal sinus, anterior and middle ethmoidal cells and maxillary sinus; sphenopalatine foramen opens behind the middle concha

details.label: Relations
details.value: Olfactory mucosa covers the superior concha; posterior lateral nasal branches of the sphenopalatine artery and of V2 supply the conchae

pearl: A pneumatized middle concha (concha bullosa) or nasal polyps arising from the middle meatus block the osteomeatal unit and cause recurrent frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoid sinusitis.

name: Alveolar process of maxilla
function: Thick horseshoe-shaped ridge of the maxilla that carries the sockets of the upper teeth and forms the floor of the maxillary sinus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior border of the body of the maxilla, from the intermaxillary suture to the tuberosity of the maxilla behind the last molar

details.label: Key features
details.value: Sockets for the 16 upper teeth; tuberosity of the maxilla with the posterior superior alveolar foramina on the infratemporal surface above it; roots of the molars and premolars project toward the maxillary sinus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior, middle and posterior superior alveolar nerves (V2) to the teeth; buccal gingiva by the superior alveolar and infraorbital nerves, palatal gingiva by the greater palatine and nasopalatine nerves

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Buccinator (outer surface opposite the molars), upper lip muscles near the incisive fossa

pearl: Extraction of an upper molar can open the sinus floor and leave an oroantral fistula; upper molar root infection is the usual cause of unilateral odontogenic maxillary sinusitis.

name: Frontal process of maxilla
function: Strong upward projection of the maxilla between the nasal and lacrimal bones; it forms the medial orbital margin and the side of the bony nose.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial to the orbit, lateral to the nasal bone

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal bone above, nasal bone in front, lacrimal bone behind

details.label: Key features
details.value: Anterior lacrimal crest bounding the fossa for the lacrimal sac in front; forms part of the lateral wall of the nasal cavity (agger nasi region)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Medial palpebral ligament and orbicularis oculi (anterior lacrimal crest), levator labii superioris alaeque nasi

pearl: Naso-orbito-ethmoid fractures detach the fragment of the frontal process bearing the medial palpebral ligament, producing telecanthus and nasolacrimal obstruction.

name: Zygomatic process of maxilla
function: Short, stout lateral projection of the maxilla that joins the zygomatic bone and transmits chewing forces from the molars to the cheek buttress.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral side of the body of the maxilla above the first molar, separating its anterior and infratemporal surfaces

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Maxillary process of the zygomatic bone (zygomaticomaxillary suture)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Forms the lateral part of the infraorbital margin and the zygomatic recess of the maxillary sinus extends into it

details.label: Relations
details.value: Infraorbital foramen medially; masseter and zygomaticus muscles arise just lateral on the zygomatic bone

pearl: The zygomaticomaxillary suture is one of the fracture lines of the zygomaticomaxillary complex (tripod) fracture, which often injures the infraorbital nerve and numbs the cheek and upper lip.

name: Palatine process of maxilla
function: Horizontal shelf of the maxilla that meets its fellow in the midline to form the anterior three-quarters of the hard palate and the floor of the nasal cavity.

details.label: Location
details.value: Projects medially from the body of the maxilla above the alveolar process; joins the opposite process at the intermaxillary suture and the horizontal plate of the palatine bone at the palatomaxillary suture

details.label: Key features
details.value: Incisive fossa and incisive canal behind the central incisors; nasal crest on its upper surface for the vomer, ending in front as the anterior nasal spine

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Incisive canal – nasopalatine nerve and the terminal branch of the greater palatine artery meeting the posterior septal branch of the sphenopalatine artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Greater palatine nerve and vessels run forward in a groove on its oral surface; inferior nasal meatus above

pearl: Failure of the palatine shelves to fuse with each other and with the primary palate produces cleft palate, with feeding difficulty, nasal speech and recurrent otitis media.

name: Horizontal plate of palatine bone
function: Flat plate of the palatine bone forming the posterior quarter of the hard palate and the back of the nasal floor; its free posterior edge anchors the soft palate.

details.label: Location
details.value: Behind the palatine process of the maxilla (palatomaxillary suture), meeting the opposite plate in the midline

details.label: Key features
details.value: Posterior nasal spine in the midline; nasal crest on the upper surface for the vomer; greater palatine foramen at its lateral edge, lesser palatine foramina just behind in the pyramidal process

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Greater palatine foramen – greater palatine nerve and vessels; lesser palatine foramina – lesser palatine nerves and vessels

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Palatine aponeurosis (posterior border), musculus uvulae (posterior nasal spine)

pearl: A greater palatine nerve block is placed at the greater palatine foramen, medial to the upper second or third molar at the lateral edge of the horizontal plate.

name: Perpendicular plate of palatine bone
function: Thin vertical plate of the palatine bone forming the posterior part of the lateral nasal wall and the medial wall of the pterygopalatine fossa.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Orbital process (upper anterior; reaches the orbital floor); sphenoidal process (upper posterior; under the body of the sphenoid); the notch between them is closed by the sphenoid to form the sphenopalatine foramen; pyramidal process at its junction with the horizontal plate

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the maxilla in front and the medial pterygoid plate behind

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Sphenopalatine foramen – sphenopalatine artery and posterior superior nasal nerves; greater palatine canal (with the maxilla) – greater and lesser palatine nerves and descending palatine vessels

details.label: Relations
details.value: Pterygopalatine ganglion and maxillary artery on its lateral side; middle and inferior nasal conchae attach to its medial surface

pearl: The sphenopalatine artery crosses the top of this plate into the nose; endoscopic ligation at the sphenopalatine foramen controls refractory posterior epistaxis.

name: Permanent teeth (dental arches)
function: Thirty-two teeth set in the alveolar processes of the maxillae and mandible, eight per quadrant; they cut, tear and grind food and are supplied by the alveolar branches of the maxillary and mandibular nerves.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Per quadrant, from the midline: central incisor, lateral incisor, canine, 1st and 2nd premolars, 1st, 2nd and 3rd molars. Parts of each tooth: crown, neck, root. Tissues: enamel, dentine, dental pulp, cement, periodontium

details.label: Key features
details.value: Deciduous dentition has 20 teeth (two incisors, one canine, two molars per quadrant); first permanent tooth is the 1st molar in the 6th year, last the 3rd molar at 17–25 years; root canals open at apical foramina

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper teeth: anterior, middle and posterior superior alveolar nerves (V2); lower teeth: inferior alveolar nerve (V3) and its incisive branch

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior alveolar arteries (posterior from the maxillary, anterior and middle from the infraorbital) and inferior alveolar artery

pearl: Dental caries reaching the pulp causes pulpitis and then a periapical abscess; lower molar infections can track below the mylohyoid line into the submandibular space (Ludwig angina).

name: Incisors (central and lateral)
function: Chisel-edged front teeth, two per quadrant, with a single root; they cut food and support the lips for speech.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Central (medial) incisor; lateral incisor; four upper (maxillary) and four lower (mandibular)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Single conical root; permanent central incisors erupt in the 7th year and lateral incisors in the 8th; deciduous lower central incisors are the first teeth to appear, at 6–9 months

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper: anterior superior alveolar nerve (V2), palatal gingiva by the nasopalatine nerve; lower: incisive branch of the inferior alveolar nerve (V3), labial gingiva by the mental nerve

details.label: Relations
details.value: Incisive fossa lies behind the upper central incisors; mental spines lie behind the lower incisors

pearl: Notched, peg-shaped permanent incisors (Hutchinson teeth) are a late sign of congenital syphilis; an avulsed permanent incisor should be replanted within the hour.

name: Canines (cuspids)
function: Single pointed tooth at each corner of the dental arch with the longest root of any tooth; it pierces and tears food and guides the jaw in lateral movement.

details.label: Location
details.value: Third tooth from the midline in each quadrant, between the lateral incisor and the 1st premolar

details.label: Key features
details.value: Single cusp and one long root raising the canine eminence on the alveolar process; permanent canines erupt in the 11th–12th year, deciduous canines at 16–20 months

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper: anterior superior alveolar nerve (V2); lower: inferior alveolar nerve (V3)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Root of the upper canine reaches toward the canine fossa below the infraorbital foramen; levator anguli oris arises above it

pearl: The upper canine is, after the third molars, the most commonly impacted tooth; infection from its long root can spread to the canine space and present as swelling beside the nose that closes the eye.

name: Premolars (1st and 2nd)
function: Two bicuspid teeth in each quadrant between the canine and the molars; they crush food and have no deciduous predecessors of the same form, replacing the deciduous molars.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: 1st premolar; 2nd premolar; upper and lower in each quadrant

details.label: Key features
details.value: Two cusps; usually one root (upper 1st premolar often two); erupt in the 9th year (1st) and 10th year (2nd)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper: middle superior alveolar nerve (V2), sometimes posterior or anterior when it is absent; lower: inferior alveolar nerve (V3)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Mental foramen lies below the lower 2nd premolar; roots of the upper premolars lie close to the floor of the maxillary sinus

pearl: The mental foramen below the lower second premolar is the landmark for a mental nerve block and must be protected when plating a mandibular body fracture.

name: Molars (1st, 2nd and 3rd)
function: Three broad multi-cusped grinding teeth at the back of each quadrant; the first is the earliest permanent tooth and the third (wisdom tooth) the last and most variable.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: 1st molar (6th year); 2nd molar (12th–13th year); 3rd molar (17th–25th year); upper molars usually have three roots, lower molars two

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior alveolar process, the upper molars below the maxillary sinus and in front of the tuberosity of the maxilla, the lower molars in front of the retromolar fossa

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Upper: posterior superior alveolar nerve (V2), with the middle superior alveolar nerve to part of the 1st molar; lower: inferior alveolar nerve (V3); buccal gingiva of the lower molars by the buccal nerve

details.label: Relations
details.value: Parotid duct opens opposite the upper 2nd molar; lingual nerve lies against the mandible beside the lower 3rd molar; roots of the lower 2nd and 3rd molars lie below the mylohyoid line

pearl: Lower third molar extraction endangers the lingual nerve (loss of taste and sensation on the anterior tongue) and the inferior alveolar nerve; infection from lower molar roots spreads to the submandibular space.

name: Articular disc of temporomandibular joint
function: Oval fibrocartilage plate between the head of the mandible and the temporal bone that divides the joint into an upper gliding compartment and a lower hinge compartment.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle above and the head of the condylar process below, fused to the joint capsule at its edges

details.label: Key features
details.value: Thin avascular centre with thicker anterior and posterior bands; slides forward with the condyle onto the articular tubercle when the jaws open widely

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Joint capsule all round; upper head of lateral pterygoid anteriorly; vascular retrodiscal tissue posteriorly

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve (V3) to the capsule and periphery of the disc

pearl: Anterior disc displacement gives a click on opening when the disc reduces, and a painful closed lock with limited opening when it does not.

name: Joint capsule and lateral ligament of temporomandibular joint
function: Loose fibrous capsule enclosing the temporomandibular joint, thickened on its outer side as the lateral ligament, the only true ligament of the joint, which prevents backward displacement of the condyle.

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Capsule: margins of the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle above, neck of the mandible below. Lateral ligament: articular tubercle and root of the zygomatic process, running down and back to the lateral and posterior neck of the mandible

details.label: Key features
details.value: Capsule is lax above the disc (gliding) and tight below it (hinge); the lateral ligament limits posterior and inferior movement of the condyle

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve, with twigs from the masseteric and deep temporal nerves (V3)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Parotid gland, superficial temporal vessels and auriculotemporal nerve behind; temporal and zygomatic branches of CN VII cross lateral to it

pearl: Because the capsule is weakest in front, the condyle dislocates anteriorly over the articular tubercle with a wide yawn and the jaw locks open.

name: Sphenomandibular ligament
function: Flat band from the spine of the sphenoid to the lingula of the mandible, a remnant of the first-arch (Meckel) cartilage; it is the pivot about which the mandible swings and the medial guide for the inferior alveolar nerve.

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Spine of the sphenoid bone above; lingula and lower margin of the mandibular foramen below

details.label: Key features
details.value: Stays equally taut throughout opening and closing, so the mandible rotates about an axis near the mandibular foramen

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior alveolar nerve and vessels pass between it and the ramus to enter the mandibular foramen; maxillary artery and auriculotemporal nerve pass between it and the neck of the mandible; lingual nerve, medial pterygoid and chorda tympani lie medial; the mylohyoid nerve and vessels pierce it

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Perichondrium of Meckel cartilage (first pharyngeal arch)

pearl: For an inferior alveolar nerve block the anesthetic is placed in the pterygomandibular space lateral to this ligament, just above the lingula.

name: Stylomandibular ligament
function: Thickened band of the deep cervical fascia running from the styloid process to the angle of the mandible; it separates the parotid from the submandibular gland and limits excessive protrusion of the jaw.

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Tip of the styloid process above; angle and posterior border of the ramus of the mandible below

details.label: Key features
details.value: A specialization of the parotid sheath (investing layer of deep cervical fascia) rather than a true joint ligament; slack when the jaws are closed, taut on protrusion

details.label: Relations
details.value: Parotid gland in front and above, submandibular gland below and medial; external carotid artery passes deep to it to enter the parotid

details.label: Function
details.value: Accessory ligament of the temporomandibular joint

name: Stylohyoid ligament
function: Fibrous cord from the tip of the styloid process to the lesser horn of the hyoid, a second-arch derivative that suspends the hyoid from the skull base.

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Tip of the styloid process above; lesser horn of the hyoid bone below; the middle pharyngeal constrictor arises from its lower end

details.label: Key features
details.value: May be partly or completely ossified

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the external and internal carotid arteries; glossopharyngeal nerve and stylopharyngeus pass deep to it toward the pharynx; lingual artery and hypoglossal nerve cross below it

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Second pharyngeal arch (Reichert) cartilage, with the styloid process, stapes and lesser horn of the hyoid

pearl: A calcified stylohyoid ligament or elongated styloid process causes Eagle syndrome: throat and ear pain on swallowing or turning the head.

name: Body of hyoid bone
function: Central quadrilateral bar of the hyoid lying at the C3 level; it anchors the floor of the mouth and tongue above and the infrahyoid strap muscles below.

details.label: Location
details.value: Midline of the anterior neck between the chin and the laryngeal prominence, joined to the greater and lesser horns at each end

details.label: Attachments (suprahyoid)
details.value: Geniohyoid and mylohyoid (anterior surface), genioglossus (lowest fibres), hyoglossus (lateral part), fibrous loop for the intermediate tendon of digastric and insertion of stylohyoid (junction with the greater horn)

details.label: Attachments (infrahyoid)
details.value: Sternohyoid (medial lower border), omohyoid (lateral lower border), thyrohyoid (with the greater horn); thyrohyoid membrane and hyoepiglottic ligament (posterior surface)

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Upper part from the second arch, lower part from the third arch

pearl: A thyroglossal duct cyst is tethered to the body of the hyoid and rises with tongue protrusion; the Sistrunk operation removes the central body with the cyst to prevent recurrence.

name: Greater horn of hyoid bone
function: Long posterior limb of the hyoid projecting back from each end of the body; it is the palpable lateral landmark of the hyoid and a key guide to the lingual artery and superior laryngeal nerve.

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs posterosuperiorly from the body at the C3 level, ending in a tubercle that gives attachment to the lateral thyrohyoid ligament

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Hyoglossus (upper surface), middle pharyngeal constrictor (upper border), thyrohyoid (lower border), thyrohyoid membrane and lateral thyrohyoid ligament (tip)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lingual artery loops above it and passes deep to hyoglossus; hypoglossal nerve crosses superficial to hyoglossus just above it; internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve pierces the thyrohyoid membrane just below it

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Third pharyngeal arch

pearl: Fracture of a greater horn in an adult strongly suggests manual strangulation; the tip of the horn is the landmark for a superior laryngeal nerve block.

name: Lesser horn of hyoid bone
function: Small conical projection at the junction of the body and greater horn of the hyoid that receives the stylohyoid ligament.

details.label: Location
details.value: Projects upward and backward from the body–greater horn junction

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Stylohyoid ligament (tip), middle pharyngeal constrictor (with the greater horn and the ligament)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Joined to the body by fibrous tissue, often by a small synovial joint, and may remain cartilaginous into adult life

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Second pharyngeal arch (Reichert cartilage), with the stylohyoid ligament and styloid process

name: Lamina of thyroid cartilage
function: One of the two quadrilateral plates of the thyroid cartilage that meet in the midline at the laryngeal prominence and shield the vocal folds.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterolateral wall of the larynx at C4–C5; the two laminae fuse anteriorly below the superior thyroid notch and are open posteriorly

details.label: Key features
details.value: Oblique line on the outer surface; laryngeal prominence and superior thyroid notch in the midline; posterior border prolonged into the superior and inferior horns; the angle between the laminae is more acute in men

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Sternothyroid, thyrohyoid and the thyropharyngeal part of the inferior constrictor (oblique line); thyrohyoid membrane (upper border); cricothyroid (lower border and inferior horn); thyroepiglottic ligament, vocal ligaments, thyroarytenoid and vocalis (inner surface near the midline)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lobes of the thyroid gland and the superior thyroid vessels lie on its outer surface; piriform recess lies between its inner surface and the aryepiglottic fold

pearl: The vocal folds attach to the inner midline of the laminae about halfway down, so a blow that fractures the thyroid cartilage produces hoarseness, subcutaneous emphysema and airway compromise.

name: Superior and inferior horns of thyroid cartilage
function: Upward and downward prolongations of the posterior border of each thyroid lamina; the superior horn suspends the larynx from the hyoid and the inferior horn forms the cricothyroid joint.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior horn (long; joined to the tip of the greater horn of the hyoid by the lateral thyrohyoid ligament, which contains the triticeal cartilage); inferior horn (short; medial facet articulates with the side of the cricoid at the cricothyroid joint)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Lateral thyrohyoid ligament and stylopharyngeus/palatopharyngeus fibres (posterior border and superior horn); cricothyroid muscle (inferior horn)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve enters the larynx immediately behind the cricothyroid joint, deep to the lower border of the inferior constrictor; superior laryngeal vessels and internal laryngeal nerve pierce the thyrohyoid membrane in front of the superior horn

details.label: Movements
details.value: At the cricothyroid joints the thyroid cartilage tilts forward on the cricoid, lengthening and tensing the vocal ligaments

pearl: The inferior horn is the surgical landmark for the recurrent laryngeal nerve, which enters the larynx just behind the cricothyroid joint and is most at risk there during thyroidectomy.

name: Arch of cricoid cartilage
function: Narrow anterior band of the signet-ring-shaped cricoid, palpable below the laryngeal prominence at C6; it is the lower boundary of the cricothyroid interval used for emergency airway access.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior and lateral part of the cricoid, between the median cricothyroid ligament above and the first tracheal ring below

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Median cricothyroid ligament and conus elasticus (upper border), cricothyroid muscle (outer surface), cricotracheal ligament (lower border), cricopharyngeal part of the inferior constrictor (side)

details.label: Key features
details.value: 5–7 mm tall in front, deepening posteriorly toward the lamina; bears a facet on each side for the inferior horn of the thyroid cartilage

details.label: Relations
details.value: Isthmus of the thyroid gland lies just below it over the 2nd–4th tracheal rings

pearl: In cricothyrotomy the airway is entered through the median cricothyroid ligament just above the cricoid arch; in children under about 8 years the cricoid ring is the narrowest part of the airway.

name: Lamina of cricoid cartilage
function: Broad quadrilateral posterior plate of the cricoid that carries the arytenoid cartilages and forms the rigid back wall of the lower larynx.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior larynx at C6, between the thyroid laminae, directly in front of the laryngopharynx and the start of the esophagus

details.label: Key features
details.value: Arytenoid articular surfaces on the sloping upper border; median ridge on the posterior surface with a depression on each side

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscles (posterior surface depressions), longitudinal muscle of the esophagus by the cricoesophageal tendon (median ridge), capsules of the cricoarytenoid joints

details.label: Relations
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerves ascend on each side behind the cricothyroid joints; cricopharyngeus encircles the pharyngoesophageal junction behind it

pearl: Backward pressure on the cricoid (Sellick maneuver) uses the complete ring and broad lamina to compress the esophagus against the C6 vertebral body.

name: Anterior arch of atlas
function: Short curved bar joining the two lateral masses of the atlas in front; it articulates with the dens to form the front of the median atlanto-axial pivot joint.

details.label: Key features
details.value: Anterior tubercle in the midline; articular facet for the dens on its posterior surface

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Anterior articular facet of the dens (median atlanto-axial joint)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Anterior longitudinal ligament and longus colli (anterior tubercle), anterior atlanto-occipital membrane (upper border)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Nasopharynx and prevertebral muscles in front; dens and transverse ligament of the atlas behind

pearl: On a lateral cervical film the gap between the anterior arch and the dens should not exceed 3 mm in adults (5 mm in children); widening means transverse ligament laxity or rupture, as in rheumatoid arthritis or Down syndrome.

name: Posterior arch of atlas
function: Longer curved bar joining the lateral masses of the atlas behind; it replaces a spinous process with a small tubercle and is grooved above by the vertebral artery.

details.label: Key features
details.value: Posterior tubercle in the midline; groove for the vertebral artery on the upper surface just behind each lateral mass

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Rectus capitis posterior minor and nuchal ligament (posterior tubercle), posterior atlanto-occipital membrane (upper border)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Vertebral artery and the C1 (suboccipital) nerve lie in the groove, in the floor of the suboccipital triangle; the C2 nerve emerges below the arch

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: None directly; bounds the vertebral foramen behind the spinal cord

pearl: The vertebral artery on the posterior arch is at risk in suboccipital surgery and in posterior C1 fixation; a bony bridge over the groove (arcuate foramen) is a common variant.

name: Lateral mass of atlas
function: Thick weight-bearing pillar on each side of the atlas that transmits the weight of the head from the occipital condyle to the axis.

details.label: Key features
details.value: Concave, kidney-shaped superior articular surface for the occipital condyle; flat circular inferior articular surface for the axis; tubercle for the transverse ligament of the atlas on its medial side; transverse process with transverse foramen projecting laterally

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Occipital condyle (atlanto-occipital joint: flexion–extension) and superior articular facet of the axis (lateral atlanto-axial joint: rotation)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Transverse ligament of the atlas (medial tubercle); rectus capitis anterior (front); rectus capitis lateralis, obliquus capitis superior and inferior, levator scapulae and splenius cervicis (transverse process)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Vertebral artery ascends through the transverse foramen and turns medially behind the lateral mass; C1 anterior ramus passes round its lateral side

pearl: Axial loading (diving) bursts the atlas ring at its thin arches (Jefferson fracture); on an open-mouth view the lateral masses overhang the axis, and combined overhang over 7 mm implies transverse ligament rupture.

name: Dens (odontoid process) of axis
function: Tooth-like peg projecting up from the body of the axis; it represents the body of the atlas and is the pivot around which the atlas and head rotate.

details.label: Key features
details.value: Anterior articular facet for the anterior arch of the atlas; posterior articular facet for the transverse ligament of the atlas; pointed apex

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Anterior arch of the atlas in front and transverse ligament behind (median atlanto-axial joint)

details.label: Ligaments
details.value: Apical ligament (apex to the anterior margin of the foramen magnum), alar ligaments (sides of the dens to the occipital condyles), cruciate ligament behind, tectorial membrane behind that
