details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the anterior third of the atlas ring with the spinal cord occupying the middle third; medulla and upper cord immediately behind

pearl: Dens fractures follow falls in the elderly; a fracture through its base (type II) has a poor blood supply and often fails to unite, and posterior displacement threatens the cord.

name: Cervical vertebral arch (pedicles, laminae, spinous process)
function: Bony ring behind the vertebral body that encloses the large triangular vertebral foramen and protects the cervical enlargement of the spinal cord.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Pedicle (short, joins body to the articular pillar; forms roof and floor of the intervertebral foramina); lamina (thin plate from articular pillar to the midline); spinous process (short and bifid at C2–C6, long and non-bifid at C7)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Vertebral foramen is large and triangular in the cervical region; superior and inferior vertebral notches on the pedicles

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Ligamenta flava (laminae); nuchal ligament and interspinous ligaments (spinous processes); semispinalis cervicis, multifidus, spinalis and interspinales (spinous processes)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Spinal cord and meninges within; spinal nerves leave above the pedicle of the same-numbered vertebra (C8 below C7)

pearl: A clay-shoveler fracture is an avulsion of the C7 (or C6) spinous process; decompressive laminectomy removes the laminae and spinous processes for cervical spondylotic myelopathy.

name: Cervical articular processes and facet (zygapophysial) joints
function: Superior and inferior articular processes form a column (articular pillar) at the junction of pedicle and lamina on each side; their flat oblique facets make the synovial zygapophysial joints that guide neck movement.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior articular process and facet (faces up and back); inferior articular process and facet (faces down and forward)

details.label: Location
details.value: From C2–C3 down to C7–T1, behind the transverse processes; the C1–C2 lateral atlanto-axial joints lie further forward

details.label: Key features
details.value: Facets slope about 45 degrees, permitting flexion, extension, lateral flexion and rotation; each joint forms the posterior wall of an intervertebral foramen

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Medial branches of the posterior rami of the cervical spinal nerves

pearl: Flexion–rotation injury can lock an inferior facet in front of the one below (jumped facet); unilateral dislocation shifts the body less than half its width, bilateral dislocation more than half and usually damages the cord.

name: Cervical transverse process (anterior and posterior tubercles)
function: Short lateral process of a cervical vertebra pierced by the transverse foramen; its two tubercles anchor the scalene and prevertebral muscles and its gutter carries the emerging spinal nerve.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior tubercle (costal element; largest at C6 as the carotid tubercle, inconspicuous at C7); posterior tubercle (true transverse element); costal lamella joining them in front of the groove; groove for the spinal nerve; transverse foramen medially

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Anterior tubercles: scalenus anterior, longus capitis, longus colli; posterior tubercles: scalenus medius and posterior, levator scapulae, splenius cervicis, longissimus and iliocostalis cervicis

details.label: Contents
details.value: Transverse foramen – vertebral artery (C6 upward), vertebral veins and sympathetic plexus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior ramus of the spinal nerve passes laterally behind the vertebral artery in the groove; roots of the brachial plexus emerge between the tubercles, between scalenus anterior and medius

pearl: An enlarged costal element of C7 forms a cervical rib, which can compress the lower trunk of the brachial plexus and the subclavian artery (thoracic outlet syndrome).

name: Cervical intervertebral discs (anulus fibrosus and nucleus pulposus)
function: Fibrocartilaginous joints between adjacent vertebral bodies from C2–C3 to C7–T1; they bear load, absorb shock and allow movement. There is no disc between the occiput and atlas or between the atlas and axis.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anulus fibrosus (outer concentric lamellae of fibrocartilage binding the bodies); nucleus pulposus (gelatinous core, remnant of the notochord)

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the vertebral bodies of C2–C3, C3–C4, C4–C5, C5–C6, C6–C7 and C7–T1; thicker in front, contributing to cervical lordosis

details.label: Relations
details.value: Uncovertebral joints at the posterolateral margins; anterior longitudinal ligament in front; posterior longitudinal ligament and spinal cord behind; intervertebral foramen and spinal nerve posterolaterally

details.label: Key features
details.value: Avascular in the adult, nourished by diffusion through the vertebral end plates; only the outer anulus is innervated

pearl: Cervical disc herniation is most common at C5–C6 and C6–C7 and compresses the root numbered for the lower vertebra (C6 and C7 respectively); central herniation causes myelopathy.

name: T1 vertebra
function: First thoracic vertebra, transitional between the neck and thorax; it carries the first rib, forms the back of the thoracic inlet and its spine is usually as prominent as that of C7.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Body (cervical-like, with uncinate processes; complete superior costal facet for the head of the 1st rib and an inferior demifacet for the 2nd); pedicles; laminae; transverse processes with transverse costal facets for the tubercle of the 1st rib; superior and inferior articular processes; long, nearly horizontal spinous process

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: C7 above and T2 below (discs and facet joints); head and tubercle of the 1st rib

details.label: Relations
details.value: Stellate (cervicothoracic) ganglion lies in front of the neck of the 1st rib beside the body; T1 anterior ramus crosses the neck of the 1st rib to join the brachial plexus; apex of the lung and subclavian vessels anterolaterally

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Longus colli (body); trapezius, rhomboid minor, serratus posterior superior and splenius (spinous process)

pearl: An apical (Pancoast) lung tumor invades the structures beside T1, giving shoulder and ulnar-side arm pain from the lower trunk and Horner syndrome from the stellate ganglion.

name: Clavicle
function: S-shaped strut connecting the sternum to the scapula; it forms the anterior boundary of the root of the neck and the base of the posterior triangle and gives origin to sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Sternal (medial) end – sternoclavicular joint; shaft – medial two-thirds convex forward, lateral third concave forward; acromial (lateral) end – acromioclavicular joint

details.label: Location
details.value: Subcutaneous along its whole length at the junction of neck and thorax, above the 1st rib

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Clavicular head of sternocleidomastoid (upper surface of the medial third), sternohyoid (medial end), trapezius (lateral third), subclavius (inferior surface of the middle third), investing layer of deep cervical fascia and the omohyoid fascial sling; pectoralis major and deltoid in front

details.label: Relations
details.value: Subclavian vessels and trunks of the brachial plexus pass behind its middle third; supraclavicular nerves cross it; external jugular vein pierces the fascia just above it

pearl: The clavicle usually fractures at the junction of its middle and lateral thirds: sternocleidomastoid pulls the medial fragment up while the arm's weight drops the lateral fragment; subclavius protects the subclavian vessels.
